security_audit.summary: Most external command and Markdown backtick findings are false positives because the skill documents or runs fixed local git inspection commands. The confirmed issue is reference documentation that writes repository state and diffs to predictable /tmp/git_*.txt files. No prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Predictable temporary files in reference examples
remediation.suggestion: Replace /tmp/git_*.txt with mktemp files in a private directory, set a cleanup trap, and avoid fixed shared filenames.

remediation.issue: Unquoted branch variables in documentation examples
remediation.suggestion: Quote branch and merge-base variables in every shell example and prefer explicit arguments for command safety.
Tell users to run helper scripts only in intended repositories and to review commands before using sensitive worktrees.

content.user_title: Analyze Git Branches and Commit History
content.value_statement: Branch reviews are slower when commit history, diffs, and status are gathered by hand. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code collect git context for pull requests, reviews, and commits.
actual_capabilities: Finds the default branch and merge base for branch comparisons.
Summarizes commit counts, changed files, insertions, and deletions.
Extracts commit history with hash, subject, author, email, and date fields.
Checks staged changes, unstaged changes, untracked files, and repository status.
Provides git command patterns for pull request preparation and code review.
limitations: Requires the Git CLI and a local repository with available history.
Many examples assume an origin remote and a discoverable default branch.
Shell examples can print full diffs, commit emails, and local file names.
It summarizes repository changes; it does not judge code quality or security by itself.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Collect branch statistics, recent commits, and changed files before writing a pull request summary.

use_cases.title: Review a Feature Branch
use_cases.description: Compare a branch with the default branch and identify the main files and commits to inspect.

use_cases.title: Summarize Release Changes
use_cases.description: Create a concise change overview from commit history and diff statistics for release planning.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize My Branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Use git-analysis to summarize my current branch. Include the base branch, merge base, commit count, changed files, and key themes.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Pull Request Context
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this branch for a pull request. Group commits by purpose, list major changed areas, and note any files needing reviewer attention.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Review Scope
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare my branch with the remote default branch. Show the review scope, important commits, high-change files, and unresolved working tree changes.

prompt_templates.title: Build Release Change Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Use git-analysis to build a release change brief from this branch. Include merge-base context, commit themes, file impact, and verification gaps.

output_examples.input: Analyze my feature branch before I open a pull request.
output: Base branch is main, with the branch diverging at a recent merge base.
The branch contains four commits across authentication, tests, and documentation.
Nine files changed, with most edits in the login flow and test fixtures.

output_examples.input: Show the commit history since the merge base.
output: Recent commits include an API change, related tests, and documentation updates.
Each commit includes its subject, author, email, and date for traceability.
The history suggests one coherent feature branch with no merge commits highlighted.

output_examples.input: Help me plan a commit from my current working tree.
output: Staged changes are ready for the commit summary.
Unstaged changes remain in two files and should be reviewed before committing.
The suggested scope is based on the top-level directories that changed.

best_practices: Run analysis from the repository root so paths and branch data are clear.
Review generated git commands before running them in sensitive repositories.
Pair summary statistics with a manual diff review before publishing a pull request.
anti_patterns: Do not run helper scripts in unknown repositories without checking the remote first.
Do not treat commit counts or diff statistics as a substitute for code review.
Do not share full diffs externally when the repository may contain secrets.

faq.question: What does this skill analyze?
faq.answer: It analyzes local git branches, merge bases, commit history, diffs, and working tree status.

faq.question: Does it modify my repository?
faq.answer: The included helper scripts read repository state and print summaries. Reference examples include temporary-file patterns that authors should improve.

faq.question: Does it work without a remote?
faq.answer: Some commands require an origin remote or default branch reference. Local-only analysis may need adjusted prompts or commands.

faq.question: Can it create pull requests?
faq.answer: It prepares context for pull request writing. It does not create or publish pull requests by itself.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should I check before sharing output?
faq.answer: Check for secrets, private file names, author emails, and sensitive diffs before sharing results outside your team.
